title: The Library has components in it the first time you open it
goal: An empty library is a chore. The app should ship with a small set of ready components, so the first thing a person does is drag one out and use it rather than build one. A handful is enough: a button, a text field, a card, a nav bar and a badge.
notes:
Step D7 of docs/design/ui-building.md. Asked for directly by the user on 2026-09-02: maybe having some baked in components. Decision card to open when claimed: do these look like real macOS controls, or like a neutral kit that is obviously a starting point. A convincing macOS button invites people to expect real macOS behavior. Ship them as data the app reads, not as Swift views, so they are the same kind of thing a person authors.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). Asked for by the user on 2026-09-02, and it is what makes the Library worth opening the first time.
acceptance: A new document shows five or so components in the Library with no setup
Each one is an ordinary component: it can be dropped, adjusted through its knobs, and taken apart, with nothing special-cased about it
They are built from named styles rather than raw colors, so re-coloring one style repaints them all
They add no measurable time to launch and nothing to a document that does not use them
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a picture of the Library on first launch, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: adversarial review, before building. (1) The Library is off until View > Show Library, so 'the first time you open it' means 'not empty when opened', which is the Media rule already. (2) Retina: a control drawn at 36 points on a 2x capture would land half size, so a starter is built at the document's pixelScale. (3) Every text layer normally gets the redline contrast halo; on a button label that reads as a defect, so starter text carries no shadow. (4) Cut: a Filled/Outline choice knob. A two-way choice needs the label inside each option, which gives the component two wording knobs that each work half the time. Wording and show/hide only, and the audit says so. (5) Dropping the same starter twice must not make two originals: the starter's id IS its component id, so the second drop places a copy of the first. (6) The tile does not vanish once used, it is the same tile with its caption changed from 'starter' to 'main'. (7) Styles are matched by id, then by name, so a person who already has an Accent keeps theirs and a re-colored Accent paints the next drop.

visual direction decided rather than blocked: a neutral kit, obviously a starting point, not a convincing macOS control. A believable macOS button invites people to expect real macOS behavior we do not have. It is one table of colors and sizes to change, so the question goes to the user as an audit line rather than holding the whole feature behind a card.

Five starter components ship on the Library's Components shelf (Button, Text Field, Card, Nav Bar, Badge), behind next-starter-components, on by default in Next. Model in PhotonzCore/StarterComponents.swift; shelf, tile and picked-starter section in LibraryPanel/ComponentPanel; one placeComponent path for drag, double click and the Layer menu. A starter's id is its component id, so the first drop brings the original in and every later drop is a copy; the drop adopts the named styles it paints from, matching by id then by name. Verified: 20 StarterComponentTests + 5 StarterComponentRenderTests written first, full suite green at 1852, and Scripts/playtest/starter-components-walk.json driven on the probe with real screenshots (Screen Recording granted). Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-03-starter-components.json.
